classification.difficultyReason: Interpret an angle of depression and use tangent to calculate an unknown horizontal distance.

content.prompt: The angle of depression of a boat at sea from the top of a vertical cliff $36\text{ m}$ high is $10^{\circ}$. Calculate the distance of the boat from the base of the cliff to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Vertical cliff on the left, horizontal sea-level baseline to a boat on the right, dashed horizontal reference from the cliff top and dashed descending sightline to the boat. No printed numerical labels or angle marks. The boat is an unfilled contextual outline.
spec.mathematics: The vertical cliff and horizontal sea level form a right triangle with the descending sightline. The angle of depression is measured at the cliff top from the upper horizontal reference.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied answers or solution labels appear.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff to the boat. The angle of elevation from the boat equals the angle of depression because the horizontal lines are parallel.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(10^{\circ})&=\frac{36}{x}\\x&=\frac{36}{\tan(10^{\circ})}\\x&\approx204\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
